title: ⭐ Practice: word fields, adjectives and a title

questions.prompt: Three of these words belong to the FOOD field. Which one is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: "cousin" is the odd one out: it belongs to the FAMILY field, where it names a boy or a girl of your own generation. "carrots", "grapes" and "recipe" all sit in the FOOD field of the lesson, beside vegetables, fruit and cooking.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses play the way the lesson does?

options.text: I play violin and I play football.
I play violin and I play the football.
I play the violin and I play the football.
I play the violin and I play football.

questions.explanation: "I play the violin and I play football." is right: play takes the before the name of an instrument, and no article at all before the name of a sport. "I play violin and I play the football." gets the two of them the wrong way round, "I play the violin and I play the football." puts an article on the sport, and "I play violin and I play football." drops the one the instrument needs.

questions.prompt: You are describing your cousin's birthday party. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: The foods are good and the musics are very loud.
The food is good and the music is very loud.
The foods are good and the music is very loud.
The food is good and the musics are very loud.

questions.explanation: "The food is good and the music is very loud." is right: food and music are uncountable, so they never take an -s and their verb stays singular. "The foods are good and the musics are very loud." makes the mistake twice, while "The foods are good and the music is very loud." and "The food is good and the musics are very loud." each make it once and drag the verb into the plural with it.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Our cat catches two or three ___ in the garden every week."
questions.explanation: "mice" is the plural of mouse, the irregular plural of the lesson: one mouse, two mice. "mouses" adds the regular -s that this word refuses, "mices" adds that same -s on top of the irregular plural, and "mouse" is the singular, which cannot follow two or three.

questions.prompt: "Our new classmate understood the whole lesson after one single example." Which adjective of the lesson does that fact prove?
questions.explanation: "bright" is the adjective for somebody clever and quick to understand, and needing one single example is exactly the fact that proves it. "dull" is its opposite and describes somebody boring, with nothing lively to say; "childish" is for somebody who behaves like a small child at an age when he should not; and "sociable" says that a person enjoys being with other people, which this fact does not show at all.

questions.prompt: Read this paragraph: "We keep three animals at home. My little brother feeds the bird before school and changes its water every Sunday. The cat sleeps on my bed all winter and only wakes up for her plate of fish. Our dog is the noisiest of the three, and my grandmother laughs at him while she is cooking." Your book offers eight possible titles. Which one fits this paragraph?
questions.explanation: "Pets" is the title: the three animals of the house hold every sentence together, the bird, the cat and the dog. "Cooking" and "My grandparents" each cover the last clause alone, and one detail is never the main idea, while "Leisure activities" is so wide that it would fit almost any paragraph.
